key.title: The key is in the link. <shine>The server never gets it.</shine>
key.lead: Browsers never send the part of a link after the #. SkySend puts a random secret there and derives every key from it in your browser, with HKDF-SHA256.
key.howItWorks: Try it on How it works
key.hostText: Where the share lives. Your browser asks this server for the encrypted blob, like it asks any website for a page.
key.idText: Tells the server which blob to hand out. It is random and opens nothing on its own.
key.secretText: 32 random bytes made in your browser. Everything after the # stays on the device, so the server never sees it, not even in its logs.
key.clickPart: Click a part of the link
key.fileKey: Encrypts the file in 64 KB records
key.authToken: Proves to the server that you hold the link
key.ownerToken: Lets the uploader delete the share

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: Can the server read my files or notes?
faq.a1: No. Every file and note is encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM before it is uploaded. The key lives in the part of the link after the #, which browsers never send to a server. The server only ever stores ciphertext.
faq.a2: No. Open an instance and share. My Links keeps your shares in this browser. If you run an instance, you can require an OIDC sign-in before anyone may share or create requests.
faq.q3: What happens when a share expires?
faq.a3: The server deletes the encrypted blob once its time runs out or its download limit is used up. A note set to burn after reading is gone after the first view.
faq.a4: SkySend is made to run on your own server as one Docker image. Without a server, use one of the public instances, which run the same open code.
faq.q5: What can I share besides files?
faq.a5: Notes made of blocks: text and Markdown, passwords, code and SSH keys, in any combination. With a request, someone else sends you files or a filled-in note that only you can open.
faq.a6: AGPL-3.0. The whole source, the crypto design included, is on GitHub.

report.flowOperatorText: Its abuse contact gets an email.

report.hintNotShare: This is not a file, note or request link.
